text.content:
The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} sorcerers claim to be the eldest organized blood magicians of any clan, originating in the Second City as mortal wizards enlisted alongside the judges as interrogators, seekers of truth, and hunters of demons. After the Second City's fall their role expanded to magical communication, weather sorcery for mortal herds, and combat against Cainite and supernatural threats alike; during the Long Night they spearheaded @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} incursions into Europe and later became the clan's first line of defense against the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere}.

Nickname: Mags (singular "Magus"); sometimes called "viziers" by outsiders, since the clan has historically obscured the distinction between its two non-warrior castes.

Caste Disciplines: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} Sorcery, Obfuscate, Quietus

Sect: Sorcerers are split evenly between al-Ashrad's schismatics and Alamut's loyalists, with very few having joined the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} historically.

Background: The sorcerers select strong-willed, disciplined progeny able to grasp abstract concepts, usually with above-average education (which can be supplied post-Embrace). Magical potential is not required, as the caste is composed of scientists and scholars as much as magicians.

@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.rules-reference.JournalEntry.9b2d10b4317f4b02]{Character Creation}: Sorcerers favor Mental Attributes and high Willpower; almost every sorcerer has some level of Academics and Occult. Most enjoy a Mentor and often have Contacts or Allies in their field. Most sorcerers follow Humanity, with a moderate number of Path of Blood adherents among loyalists.

Prior to the Schism, the sorcerers maintained a loose meritocracy based on skill and academic descent; status came from a sorcerer's own abilities and the credentials of his teachers. Both loyalists and schismatics follow the pre-Schism tradition of appointing the Amr (caste head) through ritual divination every year. Al-Ashrad heads the schismatics; the loyalist sorcerers generally acknowledge his childe and protégé, Amaravati, as their Amr.

Bloodlines: No known variations exist among modern sorcerers, though historical records show the caste was once predisposed to Auspex rather than Obfuscate, a shift that took place between the 12th and 15th centuries.

Note on caste weaknesses: See the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} Caste Weaknesses (Variant Rules) entry in the rules reference for the optional Storyteller systems governing sorcerer-specific weaknesses (stained blood-magic auras and vulnerability to supernatural perception).
